title: Joint continuity of the product density Hessian
statement: Let $I$ be a finite set and let $v\ge 0$. The product Gaussian density Hessian, viewed as a continuous bilinear form on $\mathbb R^I$, is jointly continuous as a function of its mean vector $c\in\mathbb R^I$ and input vector $z\in\mathbb R^I$.
replaced: Let $I$ be finite and $v\ge0$. Put $G_v(c,z)=\prod_i p_v(c_i,z_i)$, where $p_v$ is the Gaussian density of variance $v$ for $v>0$ and $p_0=0$, and put $S_v(c,z)[h]=\sum_i((z_i-c_i)/v)h_i$, with division by zero equal to zero. Define $A_v(c,z)[h]=G_v(c,z)S_v(c,z)[h]$ and $T_v(c,z)[h,k]=G_v(c,z)(S_v(c,z)[h]S_v(c,z)[k]-\sum_i h_i k_i/v)$. For fixed $v\ge0$, the map $(c,z)\mapsto T_v(c,z)$ is continuous in bilinear operator norm.
